text:
Rae: heads-up after today's routing tweak users saw tiny duplicate session rows in the console around reconnects. looks like soft-close -> immediate reconnect -> new claim before old tombstone clears.
Ben: saw the spike on dashboard. is this SSE-only?
Rae: mostly SSE; a handful of WS multiplexed flows too. quick log: [proxy] claim id=u123 ttl=60ms; [client] close 1000; [client] reconnect -> new claim 250ms later; billing recorded two charge-starts 250ms apart.
Noor: billing charges on claim start, so overlapping claims == overlapping charges. Did we change affinity TTL in the canary?
Rae: yes, we tightened affinity splay yesterday. intended to reduce hot-shard tail but side-effect is more route flips on immediate reconnects.
infra-billing: noted. Options: 1) delay charge until first byte (complicates failed handshakes), 2) add short idempotency window keyed by fingerprint, 3) rely on Last-Event-ID from clients for dedupe.
Ben: (2) sounds pragmatic. fingerprint = client-id + low-res IP + UA hash. Caveats: NAT & shared IPs can cause false dedupe.
Noor: short-term mitigation: console should hide overlaps <500ms and annotate as "likely route-swap" with link to trace. that reduces support noise while infra patches.
Rae: agree. I'll revert the affinity change on canary now and open RFC for billing idempotency with a 1s soft window and Last-Event-ID precedence.
Ben: also add telemetry: "route_claim_overlap_rate" and histogram of overlap durations plus top-k fingerprints. alert if >0.2% in 5m.
infra-billing: will prototype idempotent-charge on staging and simulate dup-connections to validate false-positive risk.
deploy-bot: canary rollback started by Rae at 15:42 UTC.
